facts.name: King Kong Left
facts.windOffshore: NNE (surfnerd wind exposure NNW - ENE, "Offshore from NNE"); NE (surfnerd guide text: "northeast (NE) offshore wind")
facts.notes: Surfnerd overview: King Kong Left is a left-hand reef wave on Fiji's Kadavu Island, breaking where a notch interrupts an otherwise straight fringing reef. That gap wedges the swell into a horseshoe peak that opens up and barrels almost immediately, backs off through the middle, then pitches again on the shallow inside. It's a short ride, but it holds great shape when it's small and turns into wild tubes once the swell gets over 6-8ft (2-2.5m). The wave breaks over live coral, so keep that in mind on the inside section. Skill (surfnerd): Intermediate. Access (surfnerd): Getting to Kadavu means an extra flight and the added expense that comes with it, but the payoff is crowd-free line-ups and a spectacular light-aircraft run over Frigates before landing on the short, narrow airstrip at Vunisea. From there, most people take a 45-minute boat ride to Nagigia Island (Naninya) on the southwest tip, where a private resort puts several spots within a five-minute boat ride or paddle.

facts.name: Natadola
facts.windOffshore: E (surfnerd wind exposure NE - SE, "Offshore from E"); NE (surfnerd guide text: "northeast (NE) offshore wind"); East-northeast (surf-forecast)
facts.notes: Surfnerd overview: Natadola is a left-hand reef break off a beautiful resort beach in Fiji, breaking over live coral. The shorebreak is fun for bodysurfing, and an inside reef peak comes to life for longboarding in bigger swells. The main wave sits about 2 km out: at high tide, lefts leap out of deep water and hit the reef pass, bending and peaking along a disorganised line-up. Expect long walls and tubes when it's on the smaller side, but it turns scary and sketchy once the swell gets big. This is a wave for expert surfers. Skill (surfnerd): Expert. Surf-forecast Natadola-Beach: "Natadola Beach in Viti Levu is an exposed beach and reef break that has quite reliable surf, although summer tends to be mostly flat. Offshore winds are from the east northeast. Tends to receive distant groundswells and the best swell direction is from the south. Waves at the beach break both left and right as well as reef breaks offering better lefts than rights.. Take care of rocks in the line up." Access (surfnerd): Getting out here is a mission: a long paddle or walk past the resort, through the lagoon, across Lovo Island, and then a low-tide reef walk that can take up to an hour. The safest bet is to hire a boat out and back. Other guide pins from this position: surf-forecast Natadola-Beach 1.1 km.

facts.windOffshore: S (surfnerd wind exposure SE - SW, "Offshore from S"); SE (surfnerd guide text: "southeast (SE) offshore wind")
facts.notes: Surfnerd overview: Paris is a stretch of five sheltered bays and cuts in the reef, giving you a whole swathe of fun waves to pick through rather than a single peak. The reef is dead coral, and it throws both lefts and rights. The bays sit protected from the trade winds, which is a big part of the appeal, though the flip side is that everything closes out once it pushes past 4-5 ft (1.2-1.5 m). Skill (surfnerd): Intermediate. Access (surfnerd): Getting there is the main consideration. It's only about 30 minutes by boat from London, but going overland turns that into a 2.5 hour trip.

Dangerous rips are a hazard of surfing here." Other guide pins from this position: surf-forecast Sissano-Lagoon 1.4 km.

facts.notes: Surfnerd overview: Siumu is a reef break with bowly lefts, reached through a deep inlet that fresh water has gouged into the reef. A boat makes the trip easy; paddling takes about 10 minutes and is a fair bit more work. On its best days the bowls throw good barrels and clean lip lines, while lesser days serve up shorter, irregular walls that are still worth ripping apart. Another 300 metres up the reef, Outside Siumu offers more lefts, though it sits more exposed to the wind. Check: surfnerd states facing WSW but best swell S (67.5 degrees apart); both are as published. Skill (surfnerd): Intermediate. Access (surfnerd): Getting out is easiest by boat through the deep inlet in the reef. The paddle is possible at around 10 minutes, but it isn't a soft option.

When it's working here, it can get crowded. Hazards include rips,fire coral and sharks." Access (surfnerd): Getting out means a boat ride or a 20-minute paddle from shore. facts.notes: Surfnerd overview: Vairao is one of the world's best left-handers, tucked into Tapuehara Pass on the Iti Peninsula. The take-off is steep, fast, and barreling, then opens into a flawless looping wall that runs for several hundred yards along the reef. Before the wave curves into the pass, a final bowl section stands up over shallow coral. It's often overshadowed by Teahupo'o just down the coast, and while it's less intense than its famous neighbor, it still packs real power. Check: surfnerd states facing WSW but best swell S (67.5 degrees apart); both are as published. Skill (surfnerd): Expert. Surf-forecast Vairao_1: "Vairao in Tahiti is an exposed reef break that is usually a safe bet. Winter is the favoured time of year for surfing here. Offshore winds blow from the northeast. Most of the surf here comes from groundswells and the optimum swell angle is from the south. A reef breaks left. Good surf at all stages of the tide. Relatively few surfers here, even on good days. Take care of sharks ,rocks,urchins and sharks." Access (surfnerd): Getting out means a boat ride or a paddle of around 20 minutes from shore, and it's a long haul of close to 2 km. Expect strong rips along the way, and keep the shallow coral reef in mind throughout. Other guide pins from this position: surf-forecast Vairao_1 1.0 km.

Tucked way inside is Jays, always much smaller than Shifties but a genuine, fast barrel when there is more west in the swell. Check: surfnerd states facing SSE but best swell SW (67.5 degrees apart); both are as published. Skill (surfnerd): Intermediate. Surf-forecast Vunaniu: "Vunaniu in Kadavu Passage is an exposed reef break that only works when conditions are just right. Summer offers the best conditions for surfing. The best wind direction is from the north northeast. Tends to receive distant groundswells and the ideal swell angle is from the south. A reef breaks right. Best around high tide. Sometimes crowded. Take care of urchins,coral and rips." Other guide pins from this position: surf-forecast Vunaniu 1.0 km.
